title: Walnut & Vellum — Linnean Field Journal
description: A Victorian botanical-journal layout pairing a single specimen illustration with copperplate marginal annotations and italic serif nomenclature on aged cream stock — set apart by its scholarly field-note structure rather than decorative nature motifs.
philosophy: This template exists for speakers who treat knowledge as craft. It draws from the visual discipline of 19th-century natural history illustration, where beauty was a byproduct of rigour, not the aim. It refuses hero typography, gradient overlays, and anything that competes with the specimen itself — every hairline rule, Latin binomial, and marginal note earns its place through communicative function. It is made for rooms where the audience reads the slide rather than merely glances at it.
goodFor: Species spotlight slides in ecology or conservation presentations
Herbalist or botanical brand identity decks
Academic posters for Linnean or natural-history society events
avoidFor: Fast-cut product launch or promo decks needing bold CTAs
Tech startup pitches requiring digital-native aesthetics
Multi-column data dashboards with live metrics
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the cover plate of a Victorian natural history monograph — spare, authoritative, and quietly ceremonious. Compositional weight shifts leftward into the text panel while the illustration field breathes wide to the right, creating an asymmetric dialogue between annotation and specimen. The mood is aged-parchment scholarship: no theatrical typographic grandeur, no decorative ornament beyond the hairline rules that give the layout its rigour. Avoid any gradient wash, centred hero symmetry, or visual flourish that competes with the illustration's quiet authority.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a generous outer margin (~7–8%) evoking the cut edge of a vellum leaf; a hairline double-rule inset border frames the entire slide as a specimen plate. Title block occupies the upper-left quadrant (cols 1–5), anchored beneath a ruled top bar, with the subtitle separated from the title by a single thin horizontal rule. A large illustration field opens across the right two-thirds of the slide, bleeds softly toward the right margin, and carries no text overlay. Plate number and Latin binomial sit in small italic at bottom-center, outside the inner rule but inside the outer margin.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a working leaf pulled from a 19th-century natural historian's field journal — deliberate, unhurried, and dense with purposeful notation. Composition is asymmetric: a primary text zone holds the substantive content while a narrower marginal column carries annotation-weight counterpoint, the two in quiet dialogue across a ruling line. The overall mood is warm scholarly restraint — aged stock, hairline precision, nothing decorative for its own sake. Avoid soft vignettes, botanical ornament flourishes, and any typographic gesture that grandstands over the specimen record itself.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; primary content block occupies cols 2–8, anchored top by a full-width hairline rule and a Latin binomial or section heading set in a smaller weight directly below it. Cols 9–11 form a dedicated marginal annotation column, separated from the main block by a single vertical hairline rule; this column carries subordinate notes, attribution lines, or brief taxonomic asides. Outer margins hold roughly 7% breathing space on each edge. Page number appears bottom-right, flush to the outer margin, preceded by a short hairline underscore.
